claims.text: The initial FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 alloy is homogenized and coarse-grained.
High-pressure torsion with more than 10 revolutions at room temperature, followed by post-deformation annealing, will refine the grain structure of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2.
Post-deformation annealing will reduce excessive residual stresses produced by high-pressure torsion.
The proposed processing will produce an ultrafine-grained microstructure.
The proposed processing will increase grain-boundary density.
The proposed processing will retain a controlled density of deformation-induced defects.
Finely divided grains and deformation-induced defects act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
An optimized annealing treatment can relieve detrimental residual stresses while preserving the refined grain structure.
Improved domain-wall pinning from the refined microstructure will increase the coercive field.
The high-pressure-torsion-treated and annealed alloy will have a higher coercive field than a conventionally cast and homogenized alloy without severe plastic deformation.
The coercivity increase is expected only under precisely controlled severe-plastic-deformation and annealing conditions.
Applying the processing strategy to other alloy compositions or processing regimes may require adjustment.
